title: Calculator as an outside tool and the no-hard-coding ladder (T1 -> K1 -> O1 -> N1 -> P1 -> V1 -> B3)

brief.state:
T1, the calculator outside the model, is built and queued but has not run. models/tool.py is B2 with the value codes, the executor, and the constant and result slots removed. The model writes a call as text (the op word from B2's op head, and two operands written cell by cell through B2's pointer-generator). A plain Python calc() returns the result string, and the entry 'op a b = r' is read back by the reader as its own string. Size is 3,277,393 trainable (B2 3,302,481; band 3,147,208 to 3,341,880). Queue 40 runs T1_s200 and T1_s201 at the default 8 loops. No T1 result folder exists in the snapshot.

Sealed screen (seeds 200, 201): T1 minus B2 pooled-5 >= -2.0, chain-5 >= 95, and write-copy >= 99.0 on both. Confirm (200-205): mean(T1 - B2) pooled-5 >= -1.0, its CI lower bound >= -2.0, T1 >= B2 - 1.0 on 5 of 6 seeds, chain-5 mean within 1.0 of B2 and >= 99 on 5 of 6 seeds, plus tool-off, leak, swap and split lines.

B2 reference (confirm seeds 200-205): pooled-5 73.0 to 74.7 (mean 74.02, SD 0.63); chain-5 99.4 to 99.7 (mean 99.57). The step-writing transformer gets pooled-5 mean 67.1 and chain-5 94.0; with its regex calculator, chain-5 is 96.35. B2 minus step-writing is +6.89 (paired SD 1.33), positive on all six seeds.

Reading (D0) passes: B2's reader output carries every digit place at 99.997 to 100% on all six seeds, but the pooled slot path loses digits (place 9 at 65.2 to 83.2%). The writing check has not run; it is scored on the T1 screen. D0b: 58 of 72 wrong text-baseline chain rows come from its own 64-char training cap; copy errors are 0 of 2,000.

Code findings. (1) The call cap is min(N_RES, n_loops - 1) = 7, because calls happen only in rounds 1 to 7 of an 8-round loop. The planned K1 (16 calls) needs n_loops of at least 17, or a second turn. That means about 2x thinker compute, not just a bigger tape. (2) Hand code still on T1's path: regex spans for the 16 prompt numbers, the place index from a word regex, word-regex copying for WORD answers, units-first string reversal, and calc() running inside the model class (the B3 audit as written would fail). (3) The 528 list_stats rows (9 to 11 steps) are trained answer-only with no calls, in T1 and in B2; this conflicts with the no-truncation rule. (4) B2 itself fails the zero-round leak line (<= 5) on seeds 201 (10.8) and 203 (5.7).

Ladder: D0 and D0b are done; T1 is queued; K1, O1, N1, P1, V1, H1, L1, ST1 and B3 are specified but not started. W1, U0 and C0 are queued as q41 to q44, not run. The EGE 6-seed confirm (q39) is not in the snapshot. EGE's whole model is 274.5M, so its result counts only as B2-internal under rule 3.

distinct.title: T1 tool-loop behaviour battery on q40 checkpoints
distinct.summary: As soon as queue 40 writes T1_s200 and T1_s201, run one eval-only script on the calls list that run() already returns. It measures five things nobody has measured: what T1 does after a refused call, whether its stop holds in free run, whether any call writes after a no-call round, whether call operands come from the transcript, and how NUM-heavy answer rows fare now that T1 has no NUM mode. No training, no parameters.
distinct.change: Eval hooks in models/tool.py only. (1) Add a 'dropop' lesion (LESIONS line 66, generate state-path tuple line 226, calc call site line 181) that makes the tool answer '?' for one op chosen from dev counts before the run; log the next-round op. (2) Count free-run calls written after a NOOP round and calls at round 7, and compare free-run vs teacher-forced no-call accuracy (extra_evals 356-389). (3) Stricter source test than sources() (311-321): an operand counts as sourced only if it equals a prompt number, an earlier result, or 1, 2, 10, 100. (4) Calls per family from the calls list, with the 19 zero-parse families listed. (5) Per-mode, per-split exact for the 13 families that B2 answers through NUM (520 answer-split rows per seed), against B2 on the same seed.

distinct.summary: T1 reads each calculator entry alone from position 0, and the whole claim 'the model reads the tool's reply back' rests on that. Two cheap checks: now on the mounted B2 reader (digit probe on 'add 12 5 = 17'-style strings, read alone vs after a question, plus a receptive-field check), and after q40 on T1 (thinker-state digit probe per round, joint-transcript swap eval). Together they say whether any read-back repair is needed.
distinct.change: Stage A, CPU, B2_s100/s101, no change to the model: copy diag_d0.py features. About 6,000 calc-true strings in tool.entry() format (ops add, sub, mul, div, mod, min, max, cmp; non-negative 1-9 digit operands), conditions A = reader(entry) alone, B = reader(question + ' ' + entry) at true positions, C = entry alone with position ids shifted. Linear probes per place 1-9, split by entry. distinct.title: Settled-stop probe, then a frozen 257-parameter stop head
distinct.summary: T1 always answers after round 8, which breaks Ben's rule that the model decides when to stop. First, a CPU probe on the two mounted B2 checkpoints: does the frozen thinker state already say 'the answer is settled'? If yes, fit one linear head on a fresh calibration set and test the stop on dev, with no change to the thinker's weights.
distinct.change: Probe script outside models/ (based on probe_loops.py). For k=1..8 record ln_z state and exact-match from loops:k runs on a fresh 6,800-row calibration set from a new generator seed (not train, dev or protected). Fit one shared logistic head (256+1 params) on label A = H1's 'settled' (right now, or no later round is right) and label B = strict stable. Policy: stop at the first round whose head says p>=0.5 (equivalently argmax of a 2-class head), cap 8. Stage 2, after K1-min or on T1 directly: the same head on T1's talker state, forward passes only (about 0.5 h on the PC).
distinct.why: Fixed budgets lose accuracy fast: all-row in_dist K4 is 6.9-11.7 below K8 and K6 is 0.6-0.7 below; but an oracle that stops when the answer is settled averages about 3.1-3.2 rounds, so there is room for per-row stopping. H1 trains the same head jointly at about 1.9x cost and has not run; freezing the thinker means answers cannot move (Test LR's joint per-round training leaked 15.88 at zero rounds on s200). Fitting on train rows would see optimistic labels (B2 final train loss 0.021), so a fresh set is needed.

area_summary: Ninety raw ideas reduce to 27 distinct ideas, 4 dropped. Corrections the critics should know: T1 has not run, so every T1 idea is gated on queue 40. K1 as planned is three changes (n_loops, N_RES, tape_emb) costing +4,864 params and 2.25x rounds, and the longest program in the data is 11, so K1-min (11 calls, 13 rounds, +2,304) is the sized-to-data alternative. B2 itself fails the zero-round leak line (seeds 201, 203), and the claim that computed families stay at 0 to 1.7 percent is false once word_filter and letter_ops are included, so the leak line should be paired to B2 per seed. P1 frees only 1,280 params (place rows 11-15), V1 fits on T1 without deleting any table, and mark 8's audit is blind to int() and to compiled-pattern calls. I checked plain_tf_steps.py: fewshot_number_rule, rule_apply, order_chain and seq_next are not in STEP_FAMILIES, so the step-writer's leads there come from native text attention, not from writing steps; teaching traces gives B2 or T1 a different route. B2 slots drop minus signs, so signed-number parsing only works for T1, whose writer copies characters. Count conflicts remain: 528 vs 429 long list rows, and two ideas disagree on whether the seq_cycle modulus is a slot. Most promising per GPU hour: eval-only batteries on the q40 checkpoints (loop behaviour, reading path), the variant-failure diagnosis, the frozen stop head (rule 10 stop), the paired leak line, the two-layer audit, and fewshot_number_rule traces. Missing: nothing covers how T1 would append the result and re-read question plus transcript under Ben's picture beyond the restart-position fallback, there is no test of learned task choice for practice (rule 10 'choosing what to practise'), and dev files, the skills generator branch and the 200-205 B2 checkpoints are not in the snapshot, so several probes cannot run until Ben copies them from the PC.
